name: Case-Study Proof Auto-Assembler

parameters.content:
## Find newly closed deals

Scans the Deals Tracker for any Build/Deep Assessment deal the team just flipped to Closed Won, skipping anything already processed.

## Match against logged results

Looks up each newly-closed deal's before/after metrics in the Results Tracker. If none exist yet, routes to a heads-up email instead of drafting.

## Draft and log the case study

Picks the biggest improvement as the headline, drafts the one-pager copy, and logs it to the Case Studies review ledger as pending_review.

## Route for review and sign-off

Emails the internal reviewer the full draft, then requests the client's own sign-off and quote through the compliance guardrail — opted-out clients still get the draft logged, just not the request.

## Find drafts still pending review

Re-reads the Case Studies ledger daily and computes how many days each pending_review row has been sitting untouched.

## Alert the internal reviewer about stale drafts

Only entries past STALE_REVIEW_DAYS get an actual reminder — most days this finds nothing to send.

## Case-Study Proof Auto-Assembler

### Internal Protomated tool — not a law firm template

Unlike everything else in this catalog, this workflow tracks Protomated's own client deals, not a client's system. It exists because publishing a case study today means a partner blocking time for interviews, data-pulling, and copywriting weeks after a Build closes — so it never gets prioritized. This automates the assembly, but never the publish decision.

### How it works

**A. Draft assembly (top row)** — Runs daily. Scans a manually-maintained Deals Tracker sheet for any Build/Deep Assessment deal the team has just marked Closed Won, looks up that client's before/after metrics (response time, no-show rate, hours saved) from a second results tracker, drafts a one-pager, logs it to a review ledger, and emails the internal reviewer plus the client contact for review and sign-off. If metrics haven't been entered yet, it tells the internal reviewer that instead of drafting anything.

**B. Stale review reminder (bottom row)** — Runs daily, independently. Nudges the internal reviewer about any draft that's sat in 'pending review' past a configurable number of days, so a drafted case study doesn't quietly die in an inbox.

**This never publishes anything on its own.** It only ever produces a DRAFT and routes it for two human approvals — the internal reviewer's, and the client's own sign-off plus quote. Nothing goes out the door without both. It only aggregates operational metrics the client has already agreed can be shared (ABA Op. 512 doesn't even apply here — this is Protomated's own marketing operations, not legal work — but the human sign-off gate exists regardless because it's still someone else's business results).

### Setup steps

- [ ] Set up the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) first — the client-facing sign-off request goes through it.
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with a 'Deals Tracker' tab (manually updated whenever a deal closes) and a 'Results Tracker' tab (metrics entered during the engagement) and a 'Case Studies' tab (this workflow's own review ledger) — see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Add a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: INTERNAL_REVIEWER_EMAIL, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, GUARDRAIL_WORKFLOW_ID, DEALS_TRACKER_SHEET_ID, RESULTS_TRACKER_SHEET_ID, CASE_STUDY_LEDGER_SHEET_ID.
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

The whole trigger surface is one manually-updated 'stage' column in the Deals Tracker sheet — whoever closes a deal flips it to 'Closed Won' and this picks it up on the next daily run. There's deliberately no CRM API dependency here, since Protomated's CRM tooling has changed before and will likely change again; a spreadsheet the team already opens every day is the most durable trigger for an internal tool like this one.

nodes.name: Check For Newly Closed Deals Daily
nodes.notes: Runs daily, 9am by default — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits. Whoever closes a deal just flips its 'stage' cell to 'Closed Won' in the Deals Tracker sheet; this picks it up on the next run.

nodes.name: Read Deals Tracker
nodes.notes: Reads the manually-maintained sheet where the team tracks every deal: deal_id, client_name, pipeline, stage, contact_name, contact_email. This IS the trigger surface for this workflow — no CRM API involved.

nodes.name: Compute Which Deals Just Closed Won
nodes.notes: The dedupe here is what keeps this safe to run daily forever -- a deal only ever drafts once, no matter how many days its row sits at 'Closed Won.'

nodes.name: Filter Newly Closed Deals
nodes.notes: Most days this drops every row -- that's normal. Only genuinely new Closed Won deals in the right pipelines survive.

nodes.name: Read Client Results Tracker
nodes.notes: Reads the manually-maintained sheet where the team logs each client's before/after metrics during the engagement. Columns: deal_id, client_name, response_time_before_hours, response_time_after_hours, no_show_rate_before_pct, no_show_rate_after_pct, hours_saved_per_week.

nodes.name: Find Matching Results Entry
nodes.notes: Deliberately in 'Run Once For All Items' mode -- it needs the full deals list and the full tracker at once. If more than one deal closes the same day, this is what keeps each one matched to its own metrics instead of only the first one being processed.

nodes.name: If Results Entry Found
nodes.notes: True means the team has already logged before/after metrics for this deal and drafting can proceed; false means the internal reviewer needs to fill in the Results Tracker first.

nodes.name: Build Missing Metrics Notice Email
nodes.notes: Tells the internal reviewer the metrics are missing instead of silently doing nothing -- this deal will need the sheet filled in; the dedupe means it won't be re-flagged every day, so check the Deals Tracker periodically for deals stuck in this state.

nodes.name: Notify Internal Reviewer Metrics Not Yet Logged
nodes.notes: A plain heads-up, not an error — this is the normal state until someone fills in the Results Tracker row for this deal.

nodes.name: Compute Case Study Headline Stat
nodes.notes: Whichever metric improved the most becomes the headline. Any metric that's null (not entered) is simply left out of consideration rather than showing as a false '0% improvement.'

nodes.name: Draft Case Study One-Pager
nodes.notes: The actual draft content. This is a starting point for the internal reviewer to polish, not finished copy — no case study goes out without a human rewrite pass and the client's own quote.

nodes.name: Log Draft Case Study For Review
nodes.notes: Every draft gets one row here — status starts 'pending_review' and only ever changes by someone editing the sheet directly once the internal reviewer and the client have both weighed in; this template has no separate approval webhook. Column headers must match exactly, same silent-drop risk as every other Sheets ledger in this catalog.

nodes.name: Build Internal Review Request Email
nodes.notes: This is the internal reviewer's 'review task' — an email with the full draft, since this catalog has no established task-management integration to open a real task in.

nodes.name: Log Review Request For Compliance Audit
nodes.notes: Fire-and-forget audit logging only — the internal reviewer is internal, not on any opt-out list, so the guardrail's approval result is deliberately ignored here, same internal-notification pattern used throughout this catalog.

nodes.name: Send Review Request To Internal Reviewer
nodes.notes: The actual email to the internal reviewer with the full draft and a pointer to the sheet row — configure the SMTP credential on this node.

nodes.name: Build Client Sign-Off Request Email
nodes.notes: This goes to an actual outside person — the client's own contact — so unlike the internal email to the reviewer, it goes through the full guardrail check (opt-out respected, disclaimer applied) rather than being fire-and-forget.

nodes.name: Check Compliance Before Requesting Sign-Off
nodes.notes: Runs the client contact through the Bar-Compliance Guardrail (NTC-33) before anything sends — opt-out respected, required disclaimer appended, send logged, same as every other client-facing send in this catalog.

nodes.name: If Sign-Off Request Approved
nodes.notes: Mirrors the guardrail's approved/opted-out result for the client contact — true sends the sign-off request, false means they've opted out of firm emails and it's suppressed.

nodes.name: Send Client Sign-Off Request Email
nodes.notes: The actual email to the client's contact asking for review, approval, and a quote — configure the SMTP credential on this node.

nodes.name: Skip — Client Opted Out Of Firm Emails
nodes.notes: The draft is still logged and the internal reviewer still gets the review request — only the client-facing sign-off request is suppressed, exactly like an opt-out anywhere else in this catalog.

nodes.name: Check For Stale Case Study Reviews Daily
nodes.notes: Runs daily, 9am by default — adjust the cron expression if a different time suits.

nodes.name: Read Case Study Review Ledger
nodes.notes: Reads every row logged by the main branch's 'Log Draft Case Study For Review' step, regardless of status.

nodes.name: Filter Entries Still Pending Review
nodes.notes: Only rows still awaiting a decision matter here — anything already published, rejected, or otherwise resolved is skipped.

nodes.name: Compute Days Pending And Check If Reminder Needed
nodes.notes: STALE_REVIEW_DAYS controls how long a draft can sit before the internal reviewer gets nudged — defaults to 5.

nodes.name: Filter Entries Needing A Reminder
nodes.notes: Only entries that have actually crossed STALE_REVIEW_DAYS make it through to an actual reminder email.

nodes.name: Build Stale Review Reminder Email
nodes.notes: A plain nudge naming the client and how many days it's been sitting, so the internal reviewer can jump straight to the sheet row.

nodes.name: Send Stale Review Reminder Email
nodes.notes: Sends the nudge to the internal reviewer — same SMTP credential as the rest of this workflow.

description: Internal Protomated tool, not a law-firm-facing template. Runs daily against a manually-maintained Deals Tracker sheet: whenever the team flips a Build or Deep Assessment deal to Closed Won, pulls the client's before/after metrics (response time, no-show rate, hours saved) from a results tracker, drafts a case-study one-pager, logs it to a review ledger, and emails the internal reviewer plus the client contact for review and sign-off. Never publishes anything itself -- always requires both a human review and the client's own sign-off and quote. A second, independent daily branch nudges the internal reviewer about any draft that's sat in review too long. Replaces a freelance case-study copywriter and weeks of manual data-pulling.
